why: The quote is verbatim (agent-sdk/subagents.md:186) and the cited code is accurate (spawner.ts:540-546 is literally `args.background ?? (depth === 1)` for the non-fork, non-definition-background case), but the CONSEQUENCE is false: the depth budget is enforced one layer up, before the background expression ever runs. spawner.ts:513 computes `depth = (args.depth ?? 0) + 1` and spawner.ts:518 refuses `depth > (cfg.maxDepth ?? DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH)` with 'Subagent depth limit exceeded'. DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH is 1 (spawner.ts:110) and DEFAULT_PI_ORCHESTRATOR_CONFIG.depth is 1 (harness-manifest.ts:107); the shipped host never overrides it -- SessionManager's manifest seed (SessionManager.ts:4152-4164) sets contextSeed/sessionDepth/sessionIsFork/forkSubagent/tierModelMap and never `depth`, and configureSpawnerForGeneration (pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:1279) takes maxDepth straight from that config. A nested Agent call therefore arrives with sessionDepth 1, computes depth 2 > 1, and is REFUSED -- it never reaches line 540, so it does not 'block where Claude would detach it'. The host mirrors the same refusal independently (child-session-service.ts:576 `depth > maxDepth` -> child-session-budgets-invalid). Consequently every spawn that can succeed at all has depth === 1, and `args.background ?? (depth === 1)` always yields true: an omitted `background` is background-by-default at every reachable depth, which is exactly the documented behaviour. Two further layers make nesting unreachable in practice: the built-in agent definitions carry only read/bash/edit/write/grep/find/ls (definitions.ts:157-158, no `subagent` tool), and a fork -- the one child that inherits the parent's full tool pool -- already defaults to `args.background ?? true` (spawner.ts:543) and its own nested spawn hits the same depth refusal. The nested-foreground arm becomes reachable only if a host explicitly raises `orchestrator.depth` above 1, a configuration the product never ships. The genuine divergence behind this row is the nesting-depth default (ours 1, Claude's 3 as of v2.1.219), which is already filed separately as f164; f077 double-counts it and attributes it to the wrong mechanism. Not one of the nine owner decisions in inert-worklist section 3, but the depth-keyed default is deliberate and documented (packages/pi-agent-server/README.md:86, docs/architecture/extension-first-pi-agent-runtime.md:307, spawner.ts:522-533).
correctedState: In every configuration the product ships, an Agent/`subagent` call that omits `background` runs as a background task, matching the doc. The `depth === 1` term in `args.background ?? (depth === 1)` (spawner.ts:546) is not a nested-foreground policy in practice: the depth budget at spawner.ts:518 (DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 1, harness-manifest.ts:107 depth: 1, never overridden by the host) refuses any spawn with depth > 1 before that expression is evaluated, and the host repeats the refusal at child-session-service.ts:576. A nested Agent call fails with 'Subagent depth limit exceeded' rather than running in the foreground. The remaining real divergence is the nesting-depth default (1 vs Claude's 3), tracked as f164; the nested-foreground arm would only become observable if that default were raised.
